extracted.intended_audience: communication/media scholars, advanced students in journalism and media research, and researchers studying news selection/newsworthiness
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and evaluating the factors (news values) that determine news selection by media and how those factors guide audience information processing and retention; covers theoretical conceptualizations and methodological approaches used in German research tradition. Useful for designing studies of newsworthiness, content analyses, and audience memory/use.

rubrics_metrics.name: News factors as relevance indicators / selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors are conceived as relevance indicators that serve as selection criteria in journalism and also guide information processing by the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat news factors not only as criteria journalists use to select stories but also as signals that influence how audiences process and remember information; design evaluation to capture both selection and audience-processing roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptionalization: event characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors conceptualized as characteristics of the event itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding or evaluating newsworthiness, include item-intrinsic attributes (e.g., magnitude, proximity, conflict) as discrete, measurable event characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptionalization: characteristics of the reality construction by journalists and recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors conceptualized as characteristics of the reality construction performed by journalists and by recipients (i.e., social/constructed properties rather than pure event features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for framing, journalistic selection practices, and audience interpretations — operationalize factors that reflect construction processes (e.g., prominence, angle, news framing) rather than only objective event features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on media selection (traditional perspective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier scholarship focused exclusively on news selection by the media as the central object of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should historically situate analyses of selection criteria in media practices; however, contemporary work should expand beyond media selection to include audience-side effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects on media use and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors affect media use and the retention of news items; the article explores how and why these effects occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include outcome measures in studies and evaluations such as audience attention, media consumption choices, memory/retention of items, and consider how specific factors predict these outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications of assumed factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical work often involves various modifications of the assumed (traditional) news factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to adapt or reconceptualize classic news-factor lists for different media, contexts, or audiences; document and justify any modifications when operationalizing factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological advancements in measurement of news factors in selection processes
rubrics_metrics.description: There are methodological developments for measuring news factors within selection processes (e.g., improved content-analytic techniques, measurement strategies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use and report robust methodological designs for assessing news factors (operational definitions, coding schemes, inter-coder reliability, measures linking factors to selection outcomes); consider cognitive-psychological measures when studying audience processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive-psychology-inspired perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent approaches, inspired by cognitive psychology, conceptualize news factors as relevance indicators that guide information processing by the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate cognitive frameworks (e.g., relevance, attention, memory) when theorizing or measuring how news factors function for recipients; use experimental or survey methods when appropriate to capture cognitive effects.
